answers.question: When a cashier records a payment for a patient bill in the billing app, what happens from the button click in the UI down to the database write? Walk me through it.

paragraphs.text: The payment starts as a React Hook Form state value, gets POSTed to a REST sub-resource, and ends up as a row in `cashier_bill_payment` through a Hibernate cascade from the `Bill`. The interesting part is that the frontend never sends the cashier or the bill status — the backend fills those in, and the bill's status flips as a side effect of the save.
Here is the flow across the two repos: `openmrs-esm-billing-app` (frontend) and `openmrs-module-billing` (backend module).

**1. The click and the form state.** `Payments` renders the `Process Payment` button, wired to `handleProcessPayment` and disabled unless a method is chosen, an amount is entered and the Zod schema passes [1]. The method, amount and reference number are `react-hook-form` fields rendered by `PaymentForm` with Carbon components [2]. Note the button only exists when the bill is finalised — a `PENDING` bill shows a "Finalize bill" tile instead [3].

**2. Client-side validation.** `paymentSchema` requires a non-empty method and a positive amount that cannot exceed the amount due, which is `netAmount - tenderedAmount` [4]. The dropdown items themselves come from `GET {apiBasePath}paymentMode` via `usePaymentModes` [5].
**3. The request body.** `handleProcessPayment` posts three fields [6]:

`amount` is the bill's `totalAmount` (not the tendered amount), matching the `PaymentRequestPayload` type [7]. `processBillPayment` sends this as JSON to `POST {apiBasePath}bill/{billUuid}/payment` [8].

**4. The REST layer maps JSON onto a `Payment`.** `PaymentResource` is declared as a `@SubResource` of `BillResource` with path `payment` [9]. `getCreatableProperties` defines which fields a client may set: `instanceType`, `attributes`, `amount`, `amountTendered`, `cashier` [10]. The `@PropertySetter` methods resolve the string uuids into entities: `instanceType` is looked up through `PaymentModeService` and throws `ObjectNotFoundException` if unknown [11], and `cashier` is resolved as a `Provider` [12]. Amounts already arrive as JSON numbers here, so only the `Integer` branch of the amount setters matters [13].

**5. Cashier fallback.** The frontend sends no `cashier`, so `save` fills it in from the authenticated session with `ProviderUtil.getCurrentProvider()`, and throws an `APIException` if the logged-in user has no linked provider [14]. This is the trap for a developer testing with a bare admin account: no provider, no payment.

**6. Saving goes through the Bill, not the payment.** The resource does not save the payment directly. It calls `bill.addPayment(delegate)` and then `service.saveBill(bill)` [15]. `addPayment` adds to the set, sets the back-reference, and calls `synchronizeBillStatus()` [16].

**7. The status flip.** `synchronizeBillStatus` skips bills in a refund state, then if total payments cover `getAmountAfterDiscount()` it sets the bill to `PAID` and marks every non-voided, non-refunded line item `PAID`; otherwise it sets `POSTED` for a partial payment [17]. There is a deliberate guard: if approved discounts now exceed the line-item total (discount drift, usually from voiding a line item after a fixed-amount discount was approved) it logs a warning and stays `POSTED` rather than silently flipping to `PAID` [18].

**8. Service and DAO.** `BillServiceImpl.saveBill` is `@Transactional` and delegates straight to the DAO after a null check [19]. `HibernateBillDAO.saveBill` is a one-liner: `sessionFactory.getCurrentSession().saveOrUpdate(bill)` [20].

**9. The write itself.** The `payments` set is mapped with `inverse="true" cascade="all-delete-orphan"` on `bill_id` [21], and `Payment` maps to the `cashier_bill_payment` table with `bill_id`, `payment_mode_id`, `amount`, `amount_tendered`, `provider_id` and the standard audit columns [22]. So saving the parent bill flushes an `INSERT INTO cashier_bill_payment`, and because the collection is `inverse`, Hibernate writes `bill_id` from the payment's own `bill` reference — which `addPayment` just set. Table definition with `autoIncrement` and the not-null constraints is in the module's liquibase changelog [23].

**10. Receipt number.** On the first save of a bill with an empty receipt number, the OpenMRS `SaveHandler` `BillReceiptNumberHandler` generates one via the configured `IReceiptNumberGenerator` [24]. The default `SequentialReceiptNumberGenerator` groups by cashier and/or cash point, reserves the next sequence number, and appends a Luhn check digit [25].

**11. Back in the browser.** On success the UI shows a "Payment processed successfully" snackbar, clears the form, calls `mutate()` to revalidate the bill, and invalidates the patient payment-status SWR cache key [26]. It also posts `{value: false}` to the visit attribute `919b51c9-8e2e-468f-8354-181bf3e55786` (the "pending payment" flag) if there is a current visit [27] — that constant uuid is hardcoded, so it only works on installs using the standard billing visit attribute type. Errors surface in an error snackbar with the exception message [28].

Two things worth knowing as you build on this: the payment is never saved on its own — everything funnels through `BillService.saveBill`, which is why the whole bill is re-read and re-mutated for each payment, and why concurrent payments on the same bill are worth watching. And `getByUniqueId` returns `null` [29], so a payment cannot be fetched by its own uuid; you read payments through their parent bill.
